paths.description: Homepage and sole sitemap URL; represents the complete promotional landing template.
Same sole template at a narrow mobile viewport, covering responsive layout, zoom, target size and legibility.
Homepage under the user dark-color preference.
Activated the sole “GET YOUR BONUS” form action and inspected its client implementation.
Representative unknown route to test error-state recovery.

findings.summary: The primary “GET YOUR BONUS” action silently initiates an Android APK download instead of explaining the next step.
findings.evidence: The rendered CTA says “GET YOUR BONUS”; authored Next.js code shows that when kY is false the submit handler calls a function that creates an <a download> for /img/1xbet.apk and clicks it. The exercised submit left the page unchanged and showed no explanatory state.
findings.suggestedFix: Replace the disguised download with an explicit, accurately labelled action that states the file, platform, publisher, size, and security implications. Prefer a transparent web flow and require an informed confirmation before any binary download.

findings.summary: Consent, age confirmation, and bonus conditions are bundled into clicking the CTA, while the “Privacy Policy” link points to the same rules URL as Terms and Conditions.
findings.evidence: DOM and screenshot show no checkbox or separate consent action. The policy sentence says clicking confirms age and agreement; both legal links resolve to https://1xbetind.in/en/information/rules/1, and no wagering requirements or commitment details are visible beside the +200% claim.
findings.suggestedFix: Show concise bonus eligibility and wagering terms before the CTA, link each legal document to the correct destination, and collect age/consent with explicit, unbundled controls rather than treating a download click as agreement.

findings.summary: The promo-code copy action is a pointer-only <div> with no role, name, keyboard access, or usable target size.
findings.evidence: The platform probe reports the copy control as DIV, role=null, tabindex=null, 14×24px. It has an onClick handler in the client source. The focused input also computes outline-style none.
findings.suggestedFix: Use a real <button type="button"> with an accessible name such as “Copy promo code”, a visible :focus-visible indicator, and a minimum 44×44 CSS-pixel hit target.

findings.evidence: Both axe and Lighthouse flag meta viewport content="maximum-scale=1, user-scalable=no" as a critical accessibility failure.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove maximum-scale=1 and user-scalable=no; keep width=device-width, initial-scale=1 and allow browser zoom.

findings.summary: The CTA fails WCAG AA contrast, and forced-colors exposes duplicated hidden promo text below the card.
findings.evidence: axe measures the white-on-#3894c6 button at 3.37:1 versus the required 4.5:1 for its rendered 14px bold text. The forced-colors screenshot visibly reveals a second copy of the promo heading beneath the card.
findings.suggestedFix: Darken the button background or enlarge qualifying text to meet contrast, and add forced-colors styles that preserve intended visibility without relying on color/transparent hiding.

findings.summary: The page has no headings and lacks visible focus styling on key controls.
findings.evidence: DOM and platform probe find zero h1-h6 elements; the visually dominant offer is built from paragraphs. Input and button computed outlines have style none, while the copy action cannot receive keyboard focus.
findings.suggestedFix: Mark the offer as a single descriptive <h1>, preserve logical landmarks, and add high-contrast :focus-visible styles to every interactive element.

findings.summary: Required legal and age text is rendered at an extremely small size on mobile.
findings.evidence: The mobile screenshot shows the consent sentence compressed into a few pixels beneath the CTA, making material conditions difficult to read even before accounting for disabled zoom.
findings.suggestedFix: Render material terms at a readable responsive size and line height, with enough width and spacing to scan; never visually minimise consent or age information.

findings.summary: The HTTPS page omits all audited browser security headers.
findings.evidence: The headers primitive reports no Content-Security-Policy, HSTS, X-Content-Type-Options, clickjacking protection, Referrer-Policy, or Permissions-Policy.
findings.suggestedFix: Deploy a restrictive CSP (including frame-ancestors), HSTS, nosniff, Referrer-Policy, and a least-privilege Permissions-Policy at the edge; test the policy before enforcing.

findings.summary: The page sends campaign and page-open analytics to an unrelated third-party host without meaningful privacy disclosure.
findings.evidence: Trackers/HAR show a request to revive.stats.rip. Inline source sends bannerName and hostName, and the app posts pageOpened/inputStarted with location.href to /api/recordAnalytics. The visible Privacy Policy link does not point to a distinct privacy document.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove nonessential tracking, document every recipient and purpose in a real privacy notice, avoid transmitting full URLs, and gate optional analytics behind informed consent.

findings.summary: Largest Contentful Paint is outside the good range in the Lighthouse run.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse measured LCP at 3.9s (score 0.51); the independent trace measured LCP at 3.03s. The page otherwise had 0ms TBT and near-zero CLS.
findings.suggestedFix: Profile the LCP element, reduce document latency, prioritize only its required image/font resources, and avoid preloading both large font weights if they are not needed for first paint.

findings.summary: A very small landing page transfers 227KB of fonts and has BFCache-disabled no-store delivery.
findings.evidence: HAR totals 578,319 bytes; two Inter fonts account for 226,986 bytes. Lighthouse reports the main resource and a JavaScript request use Cache-Control: no-store, preventing BFCache.
findings.suggestedFix: Subset fonts, preload only the first-paint weight, use system fallbacks where practical, and permit safe caching/BFCache for this static landing experience.

findings.summary: Images omit intrinsic dimensions and the hero person image is rendered at the wrong aspect ratio.
findings.evidence: The images primitive reports all four images without width/height. Lighthouse flags man_md_800.png displayed at 240×250 versus its 377×381 intrinsic ratio.
findings.suggestedFix: Add accurate width/height or aspect-ratio and preserve object-fit without distorting the subject; provide responsive AVIF/WebP candidates for raster art.

findings.summary: Indexing signals conflict: the sitemap lists the page, but robots.txt ends with a site-wide Disallow and the document has no canonical URL.
findings.evidence: routes.json captures sitemap.xml containing only the homepage and robots.txt containing an Allow group followed by “User-Agent: * / Disallow: /”. The platform probe reports canonical=null.
findings.suggestedFix: Choose an indexing policy, make robots.txt unambiguous and consistent with the sitemap, and add a self-referencing canonical for the public landing page.

findings.summary: The commercial offer has no Open Graph, social preview, or structured entity metadata.
findings.evidence: The platform probe finds zero JSON-LD blocks and no og:* metadata despite a branded gambling promotion being the page’s entire content.
findings.suggestedFix: Add accurate Open Graph/Twitter preview fields and appropriate schema.org Organization/Offer metadata that matches the visible terms and publisher identity.

findings.summary: The dark visual design is hard-coded rather than participating in the user’s color-scheme preference.
findings.evidence: Light and emulated-dark screenshots are byte-identical; CSS inspection finds no prefers-color-scheme, light-dark(), or color-scheme support.
findings.suggestedFix: Declare color-scheme and define preference-driven light/dark tokens, while preserving the existing dark treatment as the dark branch.

findings.summary: The APK-download branch provides no visible success, error, or recovery state.
findings.evidence: After activating the CTA the evaluated page URL, title, and body text remained unchanged. Source shows the disabled server-submit branch directly creates and clicks a download link, with only a console error/toast if an exception is thrown.
findings.suggestedFix: Show an explicit confirmation and persistent status for download start/failure, include retry/cancel controls, and do not rely on a transient toast or browser download chrome.

findings.summary: The “international” landing page uses only physical CSS directions and declares no directionality.
findings.evidence: html lang="en" is valid, but dir is absent; stylesheet inspection finds 58 left/right physical declarations and zero logical-property declarations.
findings.suggestedFix: Set an explicit direction where appropriate and migrate layout spacing/positioning to inline/block logical properties so translated or RTL variants can reflow.

findings.summary: The not-found state is a dead end with no route back or recovery action.
findings.evidence: The exercised /does-not-exist route renders only the brand bar and “Page not found”; the probe finds zero links.
findings.suggestedFix: Provide a clear link back to the homepage and explain what the visitor can do next; ensure the server also returns the correct 404 status.

taskList.title: Stop the disguised APK download and make the primary flow explicit, informed, and recoverable
Unbundle consent/age confirmation and publish correct, complete bonus and privacy terms
Deploy CSP, HSTS, clickjacking, nosniff, referrer, and permissions policies
Make copy, focus, zoom, contrast, headings, and legal text accessible
Improve LCP and resource delivery by trimming/preloading fonts and fixing cache policy
Resolve robots/canonical conflicts and add accurate share/entity metadata
Add intrinsic image sizing and responsive modern raster assets
Add preference-driven theming and robust forced-colors behavior
Use logical CSS properties for translation and RTL readiness
